method: Hand computation from this vector's input.json and conventions.json together with docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the METRIC_DEFINITIONS in src/types.ts. No metric-computing code was written, imported or run, and no expected.json was opened while this file was produced.
rounding: Half-up to four decimal places; terminating values left exact.

working.step0_payDefinition: Same map as v02 and v03. This vector is v03 plus one extra man, w10, whose total pay 2200 duplicates w05's exactly — which is what creates the boundary tie.
working.step2_sexSplit: Five women (w01-w04, w09) and five men (w05-w08, w10). n = 10, excludedN 0.
working.step5_metricC: Both sexes now have an ODD headcount of five, so lower_of_two is not reached on either side. Female ascending 1800, 2000, 2400, 3000, 3400 -> middle 2400. Male ascending 2200, 2200, 2800, 3600, 4200 -> middle 2800. (2800-2400)/2800 = 0.1428571... -> 14.2857.
working.step6_metricD: Female BONUS ascending 150, 200, 300, 400, 500 -> middle 300. Male BONUS ascending 200, 200, 400, 600, 800 -> middle 400. (400-300)/400 = 0.25 -> 25.
working.step7_metricE: All ten BONUS figures are strictly positive: 5 of 5 women, 5 of 5 men. Scalar 100.

step8_quartiles.sizes: n = 10 gives 10 = 4 x 2 + 2. Under to_lower the two leftovers go one per quarter from the lowest upward, so Q1 and Q2 each take an extra worker: sizes 3, 3, 2, 2. The alternative reading the convention document explicitly rejects — both leftovers into Q1 — would give 4, 2, 2, 2, which is not four equal groups in any sense Art. 3(1)(f) recognises.
step8_quartiles.tie: w05 and w10 share the pay level 2200 at positions 3 and 4. With sizes 3, 3, 2, 2 the Q1/Q2 boundary falls between positions 3 and 4, so the tied pair straddles it.
step8_quartiles.tieResolution: The tied block is single-sex — two men — so ukgov_proportional is a no-op here: whichever way the two are spread, each quarter receiving one of them receives a man. Q1 takes one man and Q2 takes one man. This is the case the vector exists to pin down, because it shows the remainder rule and the tie rule interacting without the tie rule's proportional arithmetic obscuring the result.

composition.Q1: positions 1-3: w09 F, w01 F, one of the tied men -> 2 F and 1 M -> 66.6667 percent female
composition.Q2: positions 4-6: the other tied man, w02 F, w06 M -> 1 F and 2 M -> 33.3333 percent female
composition.Q3: positions 7-8: w03 F, w04 F -> 100 percent female
composition.Q4: positions 9-10: w07 M, w08 M -> 0 percent female

step8_quartiles.scalarChosen: 66.6667, the female share of the lowest quartile pay band.

working.step9_metricG: One category, Ops, holding all ten workers, so the category gap equals metric (a) at 16.
working.step10_suppression: minGroupSize null: no suppression, no unreliability.
working.step11_art10: Ops at 16 clears the five-percentage-point trigger.

ambiguities.issue: Scope of metrics (a) and (c): total pay, or ordinary basic wage or salary alone.
readings: Total pay — Art. 3(1)(a) is inclusive and METRIC_DEFINITIONS restricts only (b) and (d).
Basic only — the payBasis heading says Art. 9(1)(a)-(d) report the two sides SEPARATELY.
ambiguities.why: Under the other reading metric (a) here runs over BASE alone: female mean 2210, male mean 2560, giving 13.6719 rather than 16.

ambiguities.issue: Metric (e) is a two-sided proportion carried in a one-scalar MetricValue.
readings: The overall proportion receiving a component.
The percentage-point difference between the two proportions.
ambiguities.chosen: The overall proportion receiving a component
ambiguities.why: The difference reading reads zero in every vector and erases the distinction v09 is built to make.

ambiguities.issue: Metric (f) is eight numbers carried in a one-scalar MetricValue.
ambiguities.chosen: The female share of the lowest quartile pay band
ambiguities.why: Both rules this vector exercises — the two-worker remainder and the single-sex boundary tie — land on the Q1/Q2 boundary, so the lowest band is the only scalar that shows them.

ambiguities.issue: No convention key governs rounding; 130/440 and 400/2800 do not terminate.
ambiguities.why: Four places leave 16 and 25 exact while still fixing 29.5455. The document has no rounding heading, which is the underlying defect.
